_ConnectionStrings_README: Program.cs picks between these by environment: Development uses DefaultConnection (the real database), everything else (including Production) uses DefaultConnection2 -- a separate database on the same server, used as a deploy safety net so a non-Development run never touches the real data directly.
_DocumentStorage_README: A UNC path (e.g. \\server\share\documents) is only correct when multiple app instances share the SAME database and therefore must also share one storage location -- uploads and downloads both need to land on storage every instance can reach, or a document uploaded through one instance 404s when downloaded through another. Each instance's app pool identity (ApplicationPoolIdentity by default under IIS) also needs explicit permission on that share; it has no implicit network credentials, including to reach a share on its own host machine. Two instances that use SEPARATE databases (e.g. two appsettings.Production.json pointing at different DefaultConnection2 values for parallel test deployments) must each get their own distinct RootPath -- sharing one UNC path across separate-database instances silently mixes their documents and does not fix anything a local path would not also fix. Prefer a local path per instance unless multiple instances genuinely share one database.
